To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the natural iron-fertility bloom southeast of Kérguelen Island (KOSMOS) had higher particle concentrations and a larger proportion of large particles than HNLC waters and that particle concentrations and size distributions were correlated with chlorophyll concentrations in the 0-200-m layer.
the vertical particle size distributions and sinking rates were significantly altered by the presence of the iron fertilization bloom.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the vertical flux of carbon in the Southern Ocean, which is a key component of the global biogeochemical cycle and is a major uncertainty in climate change models.
the role of particle dynamics in carbon export from the euphotic zone and the fate of carbon in the mesopelagic layer in the Southern Ocean.
the role of particle size in controlling the vertical flux of organic carbon and the potential importance of particle size in determining the efficiency of iron fertilization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mesopelagic carbon flux is enhanced by the iron-fertilized phytoplankton bloom.
the mesopelagic carbon flux beneath the bloom is enhanced relative to HNLC water.
the mesopelagic ecosystem in the bloom is dominated by larger particles, and the mesopelagial ecosystem in HNLC waters is dominated by small particles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a bloom in HNLC waters is associated with a greater proportion of larger particles, a faster removal of these particles, and a greater flux of carbon into the ocean interior.
iron-fertilized phytoplankton blooms are characterized by a greater abundance and volume of particles, and that the mesopelagic carbon flux is higher beneath such blooms.
iron fertilization of the Southern Ocean leads to a greater abundance and volume of large particles in the mesopelagic zone.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the natural iron-fueled bloom had a greater abundance of large particles and a higher total particle flux in the upper mesopelagic layer, suggesting that iron addition may increase the export of organic carbon to depth.
the vertical particle distribution and sinking rates in the mesopelagic layer are strongly affected by the presence of the bloom.
the vertical flux of organic carbon in the mesopelagic zone is enhanced beneath the natural iron-induced bloom, and that the mesopelagial is not a simple “mixing reservoir.”
